name: Proxim8 — queue-stress early
description:
Proxim8 is an illustrative 24-hour distributed-inference site in an existing Campbell, California office building sharing a PG&E service with t=0 at local midnight on a business weekday, capped at 5.0 MW. It has 10 Slurm training jobs, 1,000 Kubernetes inference sessions serving Mistral and Cohere LLMs, and 10,000 short Ray agentic API calls; all use hopper_8gpu_air. The seeded workload generator uses seed 20261102. DR-2026-11-02-PROXIM8-MIDNIGHT (PROPOSED_HERE): 5 overnight Kubernetes sessions start at midnight as 24/7 inference carry-over from the previous day. Physical sizing, workload timing, BESS sizing, office PUE, building curve and diesel placeholder are PROPOSED_HERE, illustrative assumptions rather than measured Proxim8 data. DR-2026-11-02-PROXIM8-COOLING (PROPOSED_HERE): non_gpu_load_profile_mw is building non-HVAC electricity (lighting, elevators and tenant plug loads); the existing engine cooling envelope adds modelled HVAC on top without changing alpha_max or other cooling parameters. The curve is scaled using the actual steady-state relation input + alpha_max × lagged input, so at alpha_max=0.2 its input is target/(1+alpha_max): about 0.7 MW total overnight, ramping 6:00–9:00, about 1.6 MW 13:00–17:00, and 0.8 MW by 21:00. A 1.0 MW / 2.0 MWh grid-forming BESS starts at 95% SoC and can recharge from grid headroom; no SoC-floor workaround is needed. No turbines, solar or fuel cells are configured; the diesel block is disabled. The built-in PG&E Schedule B-20 TOU rates are selected with the July calendar month; 114.82 USD/MWh is the flat operating-cost fallback.

Queue-stress early variant (DR-2026-11-05-PROXIM8-EARLY-0900, PROPOSED_HERE): the session starts at local 09:00. The complete business-day timeline is rotated by nine hours: Slurm and K8S keep their original local arrival times. Of the 2,800 seeded random Ray background calls, 1,500 are selected across the rotated day and moved into the wave pool; 1,300 remain random background arrivals, with calls left in every hour. The building non-GPU load curve is rotated by the same amount. The five K8S midnight carry-over sessions therefore appear at the session's 15:00 mark. The 7,200 former Ray burst calls plus 1,500 borrowed background calls form ten stress waves at local 09:15, 10:15, and hourly through 18:15. The engine has no session-start-hour field: PG&E B-20 TOU periods still use simulated hours from midnight, so tariff periods are offset from local time by nine hours in this variant (PROPOSED_HERE). No physics, admission, cooling, dispatch, or engine behavior is changed. The 12-trial calibration did not meet the 60-second minimum on every wave; the best trial is diagnostic only and is not acceptance-ready.

operating_cost_inputs.diesel_price_usd_per_gal_provenance: Not configured because the diesel block is disabled.
operating_cost_inputs.currency_year_provenance: PROPOSED_HERE: PG&E B-20 rates are in USD; the flat grid price is the operating-cost fallback.

grid_tariff_reference.source: core/economic_dispatch_loop.py pge_price_for_period; Cal. P.U.C. Sheet 61081-E, effective 2026-03-01.

provenance_proxim8.cooling_decision: DR-2026-11-02-PROXIM8-COOLING (PROPOSED_HERE): building HVAC uses the existing engine cooling envelope on top of non-HVAC load.
provenance_proxim8.generation_note: Scripted start/end events only; no kube_config, kube_clusters, or slurm_config.

clock_rotation.edl_time_basis: EDL hour is sim_time_seconds // 3600 % 24; no scenario session-start-hour override exists, so B-20 is 9 hours behind site local time.

ray_background_rotation.selection_method: seeded random ordering across rotated hours, accepting a call only while at least one background call remains in its hour

proposed_here: Session local start 09:00; all original-day inputs are rotated by nine hours.
The five midnight K8S carry-over sessions rotate to the following-night position.
Ten Ray wave starts are 09:15 through 18:15 local, one hour apart.
Exactly 1,500 background Ray calls are selected by a separate seeded draw and moved into the ten waves; remaining background calls stay spread across at least 20 hours.
The 7,200 original wave calls plus borrowed background calls are allocated by per-wave counts and within-wave spacing.
PG&E B-20 uses sim time from midnight, so its periods are offset by nine hours from local time.
